subject: Computer Networking
title: AI and the Future of Email
description: A micro-lesson that makes AI and the Future of Email usable.

hook.text: AI now drafts replies, sorts your inbox, and even attends meetings for you. Email is transforming.

buildup.text: Gmail's Smart Reply suggests three short responses. Smart Compose finishes your sentences as you type.

discovery.text: AI prioritizes your inbox. Important emails surface first. Low-priority ones stay hidden until you're free.

twist.text: AI-generated phishing is harder to detect. Perfect grammar and personal details fool both humans and filters.

climax.text: Microsoft Copilot summarizes long email threads and drafts context-aware replies. The inbox becomes an assistant.

punchline.text: AI is reshaping email. Smarter inbox, smarter threats, new balance.

quiz.question: What is a risk of AI in the email space?
options: AI-generated phishing is harder to detect
AI makes email too fast for servers to handle
AI eliminates the need for email entirely

details.summary: AI is transforming email through smart compose suggestions, automatic categorization, priority inbox ranking, meeting scheduling, and summarization of long threads. Future developments include AI assistants that can draft replies, extract action items, and manage email communication autonomously.
details.whyItMatters: AI is reshaping how people interact with email by reducing the manual effort of reading, sorting, and responding. It may eventually make email management largely automatic.
takeaways: AI powers smart compose, priority inbox, and auto-categorization
Email summarization reduces time spent reading long threads
AI assistants may eventually handle routine email autonomously

faq.question: How is AI currently used in email?
faq.answer: Gmail's Smart Compose suggests completions as you type. Priority Inbox uses machine learning to surface important messages. AI categorizes email into tabs. Spam filtering relies heavily on machine learning. Some tools summarize long threads and extract action items automatically.

faq.question: Will AI replace the need to read and write emails?
faq.answer: For routine communication, AI will increasingly handle drafting and summarizing. But important decisions, nuanced negotiations, and relationship-building will still require human judgment. AI will reduce email volume and effort but not eliminate the need for human communication skills.
